import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 299

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/298](https://www.erdosproblems.com/298)
- [erdosproblems.com/299](https://www.erdosproblems.com/299)
- [Bl21] Bloom, T. F., On a density conjecture about unit fractions. arXiv:2112.03726 (2021).
-/

open Filter

namespace Erdos299

/--
Is there an infinite sequence $a_1 < a_2 < \dots$ such that $a_{i+1} - a_i = O(1)$ and no finite
sum of $\frac{1}{a_i}$ is equal to 1?

There does not exist such a sequence, which follows from the positive solution to
[erdosproblems.com/298] by Bloom [Bl21].

This was formalized in Lean 3 by Bloom and Mehta.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 40, formal_proof using other_system at "https://github.com/b-mehta/unit-fractions/blob/master/src/final_results.lean"]
theorem erdos_299 : answer(False) ↔ (∃ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
    StrictMono a ∧ (∀ n, 0 < a n) ∧
    (fun n ↦ (a (n + 1) : ℝ) - a n) =O[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ S : Finset ℕ, ∑ i ∈ S, (1 : ℝ) / a i ≠ 1) := by
  sorry

/--
The corresponding question is also false if one replaces sequences such that $a_{i+1} - a_i = O(1)$
with sets of positive density, as follows from [Bl21].

The statement is as follows:
If $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ has positive upper density (and hence certainly if $A$ has positive
density) then there is a finite $S \subset A$ such that $\sum_{n \in S} \frac{1}{n} = 1$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 40]
theorem erdos_299.variants.density : ∀ (A : Set ℕ), 0 ∉ A → 0 < A.upperDensity →
    ∃ S : Finset ℕ, ↑S ⊆ A ∧ ∑ n ∈ S, (1 : ℝ) / n = 1 := by
  sorry

end Erdos299

reformulations.difference: Compared with Graham's universal bounded-gap formulation, Lean states that no counterexample sequence exists, using an eventual real-valued O(1) bound and finite sets of indices.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: False ↔ ∃ a, ... is equivalent to saying every qualifying sequence has a finite reciprocal subsum equal to 1. For a strictly increasing natural-number sequence, an eventual O(1) gap bound is equivalent to a uniform natural-number bound: enlarge the eventual constant to cover the finitely many initial gaps. StrictMono also makes finite index subsets correspond bijectively to finite subsets of the sequence's range, preserving the sums. Both the full logical/bounded-gap equivalence and the index-set correspondence were proved in scratch.lean without using the problem's sorry proofs.

reformulations.difference: The density helper counts A ∩ [0,N), whereas Bloom defines upper density using A ∩ [1,N]. The finite sums are over ℝ rather than the ℚ used in the cited Lean 3 proof.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Because 0 ∉ A, the two counting functions differ by at most one, so their normalized values differ by at most 1/N and have the same limsup. This equality and the resulting equivalence of the density statements were proved in density-checks.lean. Separately, scratch.lean proves that a finite reciprocal sum equals 1 in ℝ iff it equals 1 in ℚ, using the injective rational-to-real embedding.

sources_consulted: Thomas F. Bloom, On a density conjecture about unit fractions, arXiv:2112.03726v2, introduction, Theorem 2, and formalization appendix; https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.03726 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/2112.03726.

R. L. Graham, Paul Erdős and Egyptian Fractions, Erdős Centennial (2013), especially manuscript pp. 7 and 10 (the finite-subsum convention and the positive-upper-density/bounded-gap conjectures); https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/13_03_Egyptian.pdf.
Graham's publication bibliography, used to locate the survey cited by Bloom; https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/.
b-mehta/unit-fractions, master source archive: leanpkg.toml and a scan of src for sorry/admit/custom axioms; https://codeload.github.com/b-mehta/unit-fractions/tar.gz/refs/heads/master.

Independent Erdős problem database, README and data/problems.yaml entries 298 and 299; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/erdosproblems/main/README.md and https://github.com/teorth/erdosproblems/blob/main/data/problems.yaml.

review.notes: Both declarations are faithful to the published mathematical sources. Bloom's theorem settles the density variant and implies the bounded-gap result, since a bounded-gap increasing sequence has a range of positive lower density. The independent Erdős database records 298 as proved (Lean) and 299 as disproved (Lean), consistent with the file's categories and answer(False). The cited Lean 3 theorem and its definitions were inspected; no sorry/admit/custom axioms were found in that project's src tree, but the Lean 3 project was not rebuilt. Direct requests to erdosproblems.com/298 and /299 remained Cloudflare-blocked despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so the original mathematics was checked against Graham's survey and Bloom's paper instead. Scratch checks also covered empty sums, denominator 1, finite sets having upper density zero, and satisfiable sequence/density hypotheses. The reviewed file was not modified.
